name: Anthropic Claude Platform API pricing (serverless, per MTok, 2026-10-04 list price)
region: global API; US-only inference offered as a priced variant
price_basis: USD per MILLION TOKENS (MTok), LIST PRICE, observed 2026-10-04. Current lineup, standard: Claude Fable 5.1 input $10 / output $50 / cache write $12.50 / cache read $0.25; Opus 5.5 $4 / $20 / $5 / $0.20; Sonnet 5.5 $2 / $10 / $2.50 / $0.20; Haiku 4.5 $1 / $5 / $1.25 / $0.10. price_usd = Opus 5.5 input. Batch tier is exactly half of standard on every row (Fable 5.1 $5/$25, Opus 5.5 $2/$10, Sonnet 5.5 $1/$5, Haiku 4.5 $0.50/$2.50). Fast mode is 2x standard (Opus 5.5 $8/$40). Legacy rows retained on the page for comparison: Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5 all $5/$25 input-output; Sonnet 4.6 and 4.5 and 4 all $3/$15; Haiku 3.5 $0.80/$4; Opus 4.1 and 4 $15/$75.
notes: Anthropic's cache-read discount is the most aggressive in the industry and it is NOT a flat 10%: the page states a cache hit costs 10% of standard input price generally, 2.5% on Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1, and 5% on Opus 5.5 - so a 2.5% cache read on Fable makes caching pay off after a single read, while on Sonnet 5.5 the 10% rule needs one read to break even on the 5-minute TTL. Three cost levers a reader will otherwise miss: (a) cache pricing reflects the 5-minute TTL, and the 1-hour TTL has its own (higher write) price - model your cache lifetime before assuming the headline rate; (b) US-only inference is priced at 1.1x input and output for workloads that must run in the US; (c) Anthropic bills through AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace as Claude Consumption Units at a FIXED $0.01 per CCU, with any negotiated discount applied at the token-to-CCU conversion and NOT to the CCU price - so a marketplace buyer sees one line item and cannot see their effective per-token rate in the invoice. Session-runtime metering also exists on the Platform ($0.08 per session-hour plus tokens), which is a different billing shape from raw API calls. No GPU hourly rate and no region list are published.
